For a real symmetric matrix A, positive definiteness is equivalent to every eigenvalue being positive.
Sylvester's criterion: a real symmetric A is positive definite exactly when every leading principal minor is positive.

items.text: The eigenvalue and Sylvester criteria stated here require a real symmetric matrix.
All principal minors nonnegative characterize positive semidefiniteness, but leading principal minors alone do not.
For a nonsymmetric real A, replace it by (A+A^T)/2 before studying x^TAx.
A positive determinant alone does not imply positive definiteness.
Do not apply the leading-minor test for semidefiniteness.
